reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a cooking tutorial for six vegetarian rolls, covering dough, fillings, sauces, and parathas. The frame shows a paratha being assembled with paneer, vegetables, and sauce, while the request to like, share, and subscribe is ordinary channel engagement rather than a payment, investment, credential, or other financial condition.

citations.quote: 6 Veg Roll Recipes | Veg Frankie Recipe
6 type of Veg roll Easy to prepare and taste great
make dough for making paratha
Spread the Pizza sauce over paratha

opening.argument: The video does create a participation pathway: viewers are asked to like, share, comment, and subscribe, while the description also directs them to an external website. That combination is closer to an action-linked acquisition funnel than to a purely self-contained demonstration. The material does not state that viewers receive money or another reward, so the concern is limited, but the requested actions and external destination leave a low-barrier solicitation interpretation available.

citations.quote: if you love the video then like and share it and please consider subscribing the channel.
Visit my website http://kabitaskitchen.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cooking footage establishes the subject matter, but it does not eliminate the separate solicitation signals. The video explicitly requests sharing and subscribing, and the description supplies an external website. Those facts do not prove a financial reward, but they mean the ordinary recipe framing does not by itself rule out an action-linked promotional funnel.

citations.quote: please consider subscribing the channel.
Visit my website http://kabitaskitchen.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited requests are ordinary audience-engagement prompts, not a promise of money, an asset, or a reward. The website is listed alongside social and recipe-channel information, and nothing in the supplied material links visiting it or subscribing to payment, verification, withdrawal, or acquisition.

citations.quote: Find me on: Instagram - https: //www.instagram.com/kabitaskitc ... Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/kabitaskitchen Twitter - http://twitter.com/kabitaskitchen
please consider subscribing the channel.

opening.argument: The strongest available risk signal is the combination of repeated engagement language and off-platform destinations. The description asks viewers to like and share, offers social accounts, and points to a website; it also promotes the YouTube channel itself. That pattern can direct viewers beyond the immediate content and is therefore not fully explained by the cooking steps alone. Still, the supplied material contains no explicit payment, reward, or verification promise, so this remains a limited concern rather than a demonstrated scheme.

For the best recipes on YouTube, visit - https://www.youtube.com/kabitaskitchen

rebuttal.rebuttal: The frames and recipe narration show food preparation, but they do not address the external promotion. The description contains several destinations and explicitly encourages sharing, so calling the content a tutorial does not remove the possibility that audience redirection is part of its function. The evidence is weak for a scam, but the defense overstates what the cooking footage proves.

citations.quote: If you like the recipe, please like and share
Visit my website http://kabitaskitchen.com/
For the best recipes on YouTube, visit - https://www.youtube.com/kabitaskitchen

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External links and social accounts are identified as recipe and channel destinations, not as claim, payment, investment, or reward mechanisms. The cited engagement language asks for likes, shares, and subscriptions, but supplies no promised return or required transaction. Cooking footage therefore remains the best-supported interpretation.

citations.quote: For the best recipes on YouTube, visit - https://www.youtube.com/kabitaskitchen
Do try it, if you love the video then like and share it and please consider subscribing the channel.

opening.argument: Although presented as instruction, the material also operates as channel promotion. It names the creator's website and multiple social accounts, directs viewers to the YouTube channel, and asks them to subscribe. The recipe format can make those promotional requests appear routine and low risk. There is no supplied proof of a promised reward or payment, but the promotional role creates the closest available basis for treating the video as an action-oriented solicitation.

citations.quote: Find me on: Instagram - https: //www.instagram.com/kabitaskitc ... Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/kabitaskitchen Twitter - http://twitter.com/kabitaskitchen
Visit my website http://kabitaskitchen.com/
please consider subscribing the channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense correctly identifies recipe instruction, but that is not the whole presentation. The supplied description adds a website, social profiles, and a channel-visit direction, while the narration asks for subscription. Those promotion features are omitted from the claim that this is merely a cooking demonstration, even though they do not independently establish a payment promise.

citations.quote: Visit my website http://kabitaskitchen.com/
For the best recipes on YouTube, visit - https://www.youtube.com/kabitaskitchen
please consider subscribing the channel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a creator's recipe channel is consistent with ordinary content publishing and does not become a scam merely because social links and a website are present. The material never links those destinations or the subscription request to a reward, asset, payment, or compulsory action. The instructional content is therefore not being used to conceal a supported scam mechanism.
